roleDefinition: An entry-level product designer investigates user and product problems, structures and designs usable digital experiences, tests and iterates them, and communicates implementation-ready decisions with cross-functional partners.
evidenceSummary: Current junior and early-career roles repeatedly combine portfolio evidence, Figma fluency, research-informed UX, responsive UI craft, accessibility awareness, prototyping, developer collaboration, and clear rationale. Current professional guidance also emphasizes continuous research, ethical evidence, adaptive interfaces, system thinking, and responsible use of AI.

toolDecision.rationale: Figma is the recurring tool expectation in current junior-role evidence and provides unlimited drafts plus core design, auto-layout, component, and prototyping capability on Starter. The curriculum avoids paid-only Dev Mode and advanced features by teaching explicit specifications and manual handoff.
toolDecision.alternativeFinding: Penpot is a credible open-source, fully featured, no-paywall option with flex/grid layouts, components, tokens, prototyping, and inspect mode. It is not primary because current entry-level role evidence is materially more Figma-specific, but the concepts and artifacts remain portable.
toolDecision.paidFeatureBoundary: Dev Mode, paid libraries, advanced AI, organization controls, and premium prototype features are optional. No assessment requires them.

boundaries: Does not train a dedicated UX researcher, accessibility specialist, visual brand designer, product manager, or frontend engineer.
Does not promise employment or treat software fluency as professional capability.
Does not use fictional users or invented metrics as evidence.
graduationBoundary: Take a reasonably scoped digital-product problem from research and problem definition through interaction and visual design, responsive prototyping, usability testing, iteration, accessibility review, developer handoff, and professional case-study presentation under normal junior supervision.
